items.html:
Licence plates in Bhutan are almost always red and can easily be seen on vehicles.

NOTE: Within Asia, Bhutan is the only country that uses full red licence plates.

Coverage in Bhutan was taken by a grey Google car without an antenna.

NOTE: Bhutan is the only left hand driving country which has a grey Google car. Make sure to not mix it up with a white Google car, since they can look similar.

Bhutan commonly uses these stone blocks as safety barriers on winding rural roads. These blocks are very common and often one of the best ways to recognize rural Bhutan rounds.

Guardrails, on the other hand, are rare.
The traditional Bhutanese architecture is very distinct. Most of the houses have tin roofs and wooden painted frames, which give them a unique look.

Dzongkha is an official language in Bhutan and has unique-looking letters.

NOTE: On street view, these letters can only be found in Bhutan.

Bhutan is a mountainous country and most of the coverage is located on its main mountain roads.

NOTE: In the south are flat areas where you cannot see any mountains.
Prayer flags near the road are typically seen in Bhutan.
Thin metal poles are occasionally found in Bhutan. They are often painted black at the bottom.

These are the Bhutanese road markers, notice the yellow top and the white bottom.

NOTE: If you are on rural roads and would like to find out where you are, these markers are the best clue to narrow down the exact location.

On national highways, the road number is found on the top of the marker, but is not labelled on the map. However, it can still be used to identify the road using this table.

These signs are frequently found in the cities of Bhutan and are often coloured red or blue.

NOTE: As seen here, they will typically have the town name you are in written on them.
Taxis in Bhutan have yellow licence plates and yellow roofs.

Signposts in Bhutan frequently have black-and-white stripes.

NOTE: Within Asia, these posts are also found in Sri Lanka, India, Nepal, Malaysia and Bangladesh. Make sure to check other clues before guessing.
Most of the Bhutanese street view coverage was taken on the main roads and cities.
Two solid white outside lines are only seen in western Bhutan south and close to the capital Thimphu.

Flat landscapes like this in Bhutan can only be found in the south.

NOTE: The coverage in the south is limited to the four regions shown on the map.
The Phobjikha Valley, south of Nubding, is a wide and relatively flat agricultural valley. It is by far the largest open valley with no major river visible on Street View.

A hook can be seen on the back of the car in Haa District, mainly in the town of Ha.

NOTE: The hook is sometimes just barely visible due to the car blur.
Late sunset coverage can be found in two places in the country; on a small rural sideroad in the east of Mongar District and in a significantly more urban area around the town of Paro in the west.
Gelephu Airport is the only airport located in the flat south part of Bhutan, making it recognisable.
The Paro International Airport is located in a dry northwest valley and is one of the two northern airports.
While the Paro International Airport is located in a dry northwest valley, the Bumthang Domestic Airport is located in a wet northern valley.

lm.name: AH48 Waystone
lm.note: The waystone which says "AH48" can be found on the road from the Indian border all the way up to Thimphu.

lm.name: Bhutan white pine
lm.note: The Bhutan white pine (pinus bhutanica) acan be found most commonly in the red spots.

lm.name: Blue Himalayan pine
lm.note: The Blue (Himalayan) pine is generally only found in the center or west of the country.

lm.name: Buddha
lm.note: That's the buddha statue you can sometimes see in Thimphu.

lm.name: Bumthang Airport
lm.note: The Bumthang Airport in Jakar is located in a wet valley.

lm.name: Car Meta - black object
lm.note: On the road going up to Trashigang, you can see a grey/black object poking out of the right side of the car.

lm.name: Car Meta - black stick
lm.note: In this section, you can see a black stick poking out the left part of the car.

lm.name: Car Meta - diagonal lines
lm.note: Inbetween Wangdue Phodrang and Trongsa, you can find white diagonal lines on the back of the car.

lm.name: Car Meta - hook
lm.note: In and around the town of Ha, you can see a hook on the car. It will be very blurred, with only the top being visible.

lm.name: Car Meta - small circle
lm.note: Between the town of Samkhang and (roughly) the border between Sarpang and Zhemgang district, you can see a very small circle on the right side of the car.

lm.name: Car Meta - white dots
lm.note: On this part of the road, you can find two white dots on the back of the car; a bigger one, and a smaller one.

lm.name: Car Meta - white stripe
lm.note: In pink, the parts where you'll find a white stripe on the left side of the car.

lm.name: Car Meta - white thing on the left
lm.note: Between Gelephu and Samkhara, you will find this white thing on the left side of the car,

lm.name: DR46, DR47
lm.note: On this road heading up towards Lhuntse, you can find waystones saying either "DR46" or "DR47".

lm.name: Flat
lm.note:
If you find yourself in a noticeably flat location, you might just be in the south. In fact, that'll almost certainly be where you are.

Coverage here is limited to the towns of Phuntsholing, Sarpang, Gelephu and Samdrup Jongkhar.

lm.name: Fog 1
lm.note: The most notable place you can find fog is around Gedu.

lm.name: Fog 2
lm.note: If you see lots of fog, or find yourself in a place you'd run into lots of the aforementioned fog, and you're not on the road to Thimphu, you're likely not too far south of Galechugaon.

lm.name: Gelephu airport
lm.note: Gelephu airport is the only airport located in the flat south of the county, making it recognizable.

lm.name: Gelephu pebble road
lm.note: If you find yourself on flat terrain, on a pebbled road such as this, you're in Gelephu. (Not city center though)

lm.name: Late sunset coverage
lm.note:
"Late sunset coverage can be found in two places in the country; on a small rural sideroad in the east of Mongar District and in a significantly more urban area around the town of Paro in the west."

  • Plonkit

lm.name: NH2 Waystone
lm.note: The NH2 is this whole northern thing. It seems like.

lm.name: NH4 Waystone
lm.note: On this road you'll find the waystone saying "NH4".

lm.name: Palms
lm.note: You'll sometimes see palms in the southern parts of the country. (Not just the towns in the south)

lm.name: Paro Airport
lm.note: This airport will be found in a dry northwest valley.

lm.name: Philippines pavement
lm.note: If you see concrete pavement reminiscent of the Philippines, you're in this extension of Phuentsholing.

lm.name: Phobjika valley
lm.note: The Phobjika valley is a wide, relatively flat agricultural valley. It's the largest open valley without a river on Street View.

lm.name: Pines
lm.note: In the north, you're going to see pines. You can see a lot of them, all over the mountains.

lm.name: Recognizable road
lm.note: One of, if not the best meta for Bhutan, is that you will always see solid white lines on the outside, on the road going up to Thimphu. Moreover, the quality of the road in comparison to other roads is also noticeable.

lm.name: Road work vibe
lm.note: This section of the road can feel like road work is in progress, or have a road work vibe, with lots of rocks lying next to the road, and a bunch of sand. Additionaly, you can almost always see a river to the same side of the road in this section.

lm.name: Sikkim Fir
lm.note: Sikkim Fir (Abies Densa) can be found in quite a few places, but a high concentration of them should lean you towards Phrumsengla national park. More specifically, northwest of Sengor.

lm.name: SL1 Waystone
lm.note: When encountering an SL1 Waystone, it should put you on the SL1.

lm.name: SL2 Waystone
lm.note: In the red circle, the area where SL2 waystones should be found.

lm.name: SL4 Waystone
lm.note: The SL4 Waystone can be found on this road. You have more chance of seeing a waystone with the SL4 on it in the red part.

lm.name: SNH Waystone
lm.note: SNH Waystones are found on the road from Trashigang to Trashiyangtse in the north.

lm.name: Unique kerb
lm.note: This kerb, with grey sections seperated by a bit of white, is characteristic for the road leading up to Thimphu. Also, (roughly) between Chimaka and Chapcha, the average length of the grey section tends to be a little smaller, making it look a bit more like a square.

lm.name: Architecture
lm.note: Traditional Bhutanese architecture is very distinct. Most houses feature tin roofs and wooden painted frames, giving them a unique look.

lm.name: Red license plate
lm.note: License plates in Bhutan are almost always red and are easily visible on vehicles.

lm.name: Stone blocks guardrail
lm.note: Bhutan commonly uses stone blocks as safety barriers on winding rural roads. These blocks are very common and are one of the best ways to recognize rural roads in Bhutan.
